facts.statement: Avaceratops was a small herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaur that lived during the late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now the Northwest United States.
facts.quote: Avaceratops is a genus of small herbivorous ceratopsian dinosaurs which lived during the late Campanian in what are now the Northwest United States.

facts.statement: The first remains of Avaceratops were discovered in 1981 by Eddie Cole in the Judith River Formation of Montana on land owned by Arthur J. Lammers.
facts.quote: The first remains of Avaceratops were found by Eddie Cole in the Judith River Formation of Montana, in 1981, on land of the Careless Creek Ranch, owned by rancher Arthur J. Lammers.

facts.statement: Avaceratops was formally named and described by Peter Dodson in 1986 as the type species Avaceratops lammersi.
facts.quote: The fossil was formally named and described by Dodson in 1986, as the type species Avaceratops lammersi.

facts.statement: The genus name Avaceratops honors Eddie Cole's wife, Ava Cole.
facts.quote: The genus was named after Ava Cole, Eddie's wife.

facts.statement: The specific epithet lammersi honors the Lammers family, who owned the land where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The specific epithet honors the Lammers family.

facts.statement: In 1993, Paul Penkalski referred two earlier discovered squamosals belonging to larger individuals to Avaceratops.
facts.quote: In 1993 Paul Penkalski referred two earlier found squamosals to Avaceratops, USNM 4802 and USNM 2415, of larger individuals.

facts.statement: In 1999, Penkalski and Dodson described a second skull, MOR 692, which belonged to a larger individual.
facts.quote: In 1999, Penkalski and Dodson described a second skull, MOR 692, again of a larger individual.

facts.statement: Peter Dodson originally estimated the holotype length at 2.3 meters and assumed it had nearly reached adult size.
facts.quote: He estimated the holotype length at 2.3 m and assumed it had almost attained adult size.

facts.statement: A second skull, MOR 692, which may not belong to Avaceratops, indicates a body length of 4.2 meters.
facts.quote: In addition, a second skull (which does not necessarily belong to Avaceratops), MOR 692, indicates a body length of 4.2 m.

facts.statement: In 2010, Paul estimated that a four-meter-long Avaceratops would weigh one tonne.
facts.quote: Paul in 2010 estimated the weight of a four-metre-long animal at one tonne.

facts.statement: The squamosal element at the front of the frill is large and features a continuously curving edge rather than a stepped one.
facts.quote: The squamosal, the element at the front of the frill side, is large with a continuously curving instead of a stepped edge.

facts.statement: A 2013 phylogenetic analysis by Sampson et al. found Avaceratops to be the sister taxon of the genus Nasutoceratops.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis performed by Sampson et al. (2013) found that Avaceratops was the sister taxon of the new genus Nasutoceratops, described and named in 2013.

facts.statement: Avaceratops was a herbivore, feeding on plants like ferns, cycads, and conifers that were predominant during the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Avaceratops, like all ceratopsians, was a herbivore.

facts.statement: Avaceratops lived in a heavily forested and wet habitat.
facts.quote: The habitat of Avaceratops was heavily forested and wet.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Avaceratops might represent a juvenile or subadult individual.
facts.quote: The type specimen might represent a juvenile or a subadult individual.

facts.statement: Avaceratops lived at the end of the Cretaceous Period, approximately 80 million years ago, during the Campanian stage in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 80 million years ago, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es América del Norte.

facts.statement: The first remains of Avaceratops were found by fossil dealer Eddie Cole in the Judith River Formation of Montana in 1981.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Avaceratops fueron encontrados por el comerciante de fósiles Eddie Cole en la Formación Judith River de Montana, en 1981

facts.statement: The fossil was formally named and described by Dodson in 1986 as the type species Avaceratops lammersi.
facts.quote: El fósil fue formalmente nombrado y descrito por Dodson en 1986 llamando la especie tipo Avaceratops lammersi

facts.statement: The genus name honors Ava Cole, the wife of the fossil dealer Eddie Cole.
facts.quote: El género fue nombrado en honor a Ava Cole, la esposa de Eddie

facts.statement: The holotype specimen ANSP 15800 consists of a partial skeleton including the lower skull, left lower jaw, vertebrae, a complete shoulder girdle, and most elements of the fore and hind limbs.
facts.quote: El holotipo , ANSP 15800, se compone de un esqueleto parcial que contiene la parte baja del cráneo, una mandíbula inferior izquierdo, vértebras, una cintura escapular completa y la mayoría de los elementos de miembros anteriores y posteriores

facts.statement: In 1999, Penkalski and Dodson described a second skull, MOR 692, belonging to an adult individual.
facts.quote: En 1999, Penkalski y Dodson describen un segundo cráneo, MOR 692, de nuevo de un adulto

facts.statement: The assignment of the second skull to Avaceratops has been questioned due to differences in relative chronological position, skull morphology, and the lack of intermediate forms.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la asignación de la segunda a Avaceratops ha sido cuestionada debido a diferencias en la posición relativa cronológico, morfología cráneo, y la falta de formas intermedias

facts.statement: Dodson assigned Avaceratops to the family Ceratopsidae within the order Ceratopsia in 1986.
facts.quote: Avaceratops fue por Dodson en 1986 asignado a Ceratopsidae dentro del Ceratopsia

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis by Sampson et al. in 2013 found that Avaceratops was the sister taxon to the newly described genus Nasutoceratops.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético realizado por Sampson et al. en 2013 encontró que Avaceratops era el taxón hermano del nuevo género Nasutoceratops, descrito y nombrado en 2013

facts.statement: The clade containing Avaceratops and Nasutoceratops was named Nasutoceratopsini in 2016.
facts.quote: Este clado que contenía Avaceratops y Nasutoceratops fue nombrado Nasutoceratopsini en 2016

facts.statement: Avaceratops lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Like all ceratopsians, Avaceratops was a herbivore.
facts.quote: Avaceratops, como todos los ceratopsios, era un herbívoro

facts.statement: The animal likely used its sharp beak to bite leaves or needles from plants.
facts.quote: El animal habría usado su agudo pico para morder las hojas o agujas de las plantas

facts.statement: The habitat of Avaceratops was primarily wet forests.
facts.quote: El hábitat de Avaceratops era principalmente de bosques húmedos
